Applied 13 as fail-safe SKILL.md additions (Verbs section: eval selector engines, type's unquoted selector, punctuation key names; the SPA-duplicate/:visible section: hidden pages inside eval, structural filters; new Traps bullets: block LiveReload with addInitScript, safe() wrapper for hand-rolled probes, crawl watchdogs, click(text=) matching prose, before/after diffs on a live page, tree selector scoping, fake-audio silence loop; a known drive.mjs offscreen-x bug documented). layout: 15 entries. Applied 10, consolidating the biggest finding of the whole sweep: THREE separate entries (2026-09-01, two on 2026-09-17, 2026-09-19) all independently rediscovered that grid-auto-fill picks its column count from track width, blind to how many cards exist, and that a KNOWN count wants explicit container-query breakpoints while an UNKNOWN/variable count wants auto-fit, never auto-fill -- rewrote the two places in SKILL.md that gave the old, self-contradicting advice ('walls take grid auto-fill') into one corrected paragraph each, citing all three. Also applied: a fixed-overlay padding rule, an auto-scroll-is-a-decision note, an overflow-scan exclude list, a 'holds its measure and centres' qualifier, and two caveats.md additions (scroll-margin-top in rem not em; document.fonts.ready before measuring em-widths). Left 1 as a PROPOSAL (kept in improvements.md, marked): adding a sixth check to the five-question ritual (how far a control's visible consequence lands from it) -- that changes what every future agent is required to answer, so it needs the owner's yes. Deleted 4 as obsolete: one (2026-08-17) was already 'declined' in its own text before tonight; three (2026-09-01 spacing rules, 2026-09-06 nav-fat rewrite, 2026-09-17 Q1 catalog fix) described fixes that are ALREADY verbatim in the current SKILL.md text -- re-applying them would have been a no-op. 10+1+4=15.

css: 11 entries, all genuinely new fail-safe corrections (no overlap with existing caveats.md), so all 11 applied and deleted -- added to caveats.md: display:none losing to a util-layer utility, el.hidden losing to a display rule, var() resolving to an invalid value silently, an em-based --measure compounding with a bigger font-size, measure caps escaping a nested wrapper, --wash painting nothing on the page's own ground, a relative font-size replacing rather than scaling, rem being a CONSTANT on this site while em is the fluid unit, and a component's own font-size:var(--size) double-multiplying every nested framework control. Also tightened (not counted as a new entry) the existing :first-child caveat with its :last-child twin, and the existing bracket-line-name caveat with a newer recurrence's extra detail (CSS.supports bisecting). 11 applied, 0 obsolete, 0 proposals.

mastermind: 6 entries. Applied 2 as fail-safe SKILL.md additions: an enumerated proof list in a brief needs to name the broken state a recovery mechanism exists for, not just the healthy path (Briefs section); a warning posted only on the dev bar doesn't reach the owner when the dev bar IS the thing that's down -- anything urgent goes out of band (Reporting section). Left 4 as PROPOSALS, three of them self-marked as such in their own text: (1) mastermind should stop doing hands-on edits itself -- a policy change the owner said is their call to promote; (2) find / needs a PreToolUse hook, which is settings.json, not mine to touch; (3) writing note/agent lines every run for the v2 board -- a new required step; (4) explicitly marked 'NOT fail-safe to fix blind' by the agent who filed it -- the CLI minion launch recipe may not actually let a minion write files at all right now. 2+4=6.

log.msg: documentation: 5 entries, all applied. Tightened the 'Absolute links only' rule to explain WHY (a relative link resolves against the fetching file, not the reader) instead of stating an absolute rule the skill's own next section half-contradicts. Added, in one place, the three missing route facts three different agents each had to rediscover: notes: and methods:/properties: get per-name routes, files: entries do not (one shared browser only); and documented the simpler note()-shaped page idiom as an alternative to a hand-written doc/page.js, including that its URL slugifies from the TITLE not the note's own key. 5 applied, 0 obsolete, 0 proposals.

new-css-class: 4 entries. Applied 3: a second core module extending Page may open its own page-<module>- sub-namespace (hit twice the same day, by core/Layout and core/Section -- merged into one edit); a modifier class built by string concatenation from data needs the module prefix INSIDE the string, not just on the literal you can see. Deleted 1 as obsolete: it asked for a 'page--<name>, two dashes' rule that is already step 6 in the current SKILL.md, verbatim. 3+1=4.

auditor: 4 lines, 0 applied, 0 obsolete, 0 proposals -- left entirely untouched, on purpose. Unlike every other skill's improvements.md, this file is explicitly a RUNNING GRADE LEDGER for the audit mechanism itself (its own header: 'the mastermind grades each audit... three useless audits in a row and the shape gets dropped'), not a queue of unapplied fixes. Its 4 lines are one provenance note plus three 'useful, keep the shape' grades -- deleting them would destroy the exact three-strikes count the skill depends on to know when to change its own shape. Nothing there named a fact to correct or a trap to add, so nothing was applied either. This explains 3 of the difference between the brief's 'auditor 3' and my 0.

finish-task: 3 entries, all applied. Added the single-vs-doubled backslash trap for \n\n in an outcome string (valid JSON is not proof the STRING holds a real newline). Extended the existing re-parse-every-line instruction to say explicitly it applies after EVERY jsonl append, not only the final landing line (four hand-typed log lines once shipped with a missing closing brace and nobody noticed). Generalised the existing backtick/command-substitution warning, which was scoped only to the jsonl outcome, to ANY shell-appended text with backticks -- it ate a 74-line markdown doc/decisions.md append exactly the same way. 3 applied, 0 obsolete, 0 proposals.

new-page: 1 entry, applied. The file skeleton's content(){ p("Body."); } example now has an inline comment saying p/div/img are functions, not Views -- calling img.attr(...) on the bare function throws and blanks the whole page. 1 applied, 0 obsolete, 0 proposals.

assign.outcome:
**48 lessons applied, 7 deleted as obsolete, 5 left as proposals** — 60 total, not the 55 the brief expected (the discrepancy is explained in the log: css/documentation/new-css-class/finish-task had more real entries than credited, and `auditor`'s file turned out to be a grading ledger, not a queue, so its lines were left alone). The `SKILL.md` files grew by about **+104 lines** net (mostly new one-line traps with real evidence); the `improvements.md` backlog files shrank from 138 lines to 26, because a fix that gets applied and deleted stops being rediscovered.

The biggest single finding: three unrelated agents, three different weeks, hit the exact same CSS bug (`grid-auto-fill` silently drops a column or leaves a gap-toothed row) — that is now one corrected rule in the `layout` skill instead of three warnings scattered across a month.

Five real decisions are left for the owner, ranked: (1) a CLI-launched minion may not be able to write files at all right now — needs checking before trusting tonight's other minions; (2) should the mastermind stop doing hands-on edits itself; (3) a `find /` rule needs a hook, not another sentence; (4) should every mastermind run write live board updates; (5) should `layout`'s five questions gain a sixth, about where a control's effect lands.
